Reported by: Priya Ondarza, Quality Analyst

Date reported: Thursday 15 October 2026

1. Summary of event
Call-recording platform retained only partial metadata for calls handled on the Billing Support queue between 06:00 and 14:00 on 13 October. The fault affected call duration fields for 212 of the 1,140 calls answered in that window. Complaint reference numbers were correctly linked for all calls.

2. Timeline (all times GMT)
06:00  Shift start. Queue opened with 38 agents logged in.
07:42  Monitoring alert CR-ALR-881 raised: duration field null on recordings from station 14 onwards.
08:10  Platform vendor helpdesk contacted by Ahmed Tiwari (Telephony Ops). Ticket VH-44720 opened.
09:05  Duration fix pushed to test instance. Not released to production.
10:30  Agents asked to note call length manually on the wrap-up form. Form field QA_DUR_MANUAL added.
11:15  Vendor confirmed that metadata sync had stopped at 07:19 and resumed at 08:52.
12:48  Production patch applied by Ahmed Tiwari under change CH-2026-1093.
14:00  Shift end. Recordings reprocessed overnight.

3. Witness remarks
Ahmed Tiwari (Telephony Ops): "The sync job was reading the old timestamp format after the 07:00 config push. I didn't catch it because the test queue only had two stations live."

Lorraine Feeney (Team Leader, Billing Support): "Agents on stations 14 to 22 were told at about 10:30 to write the call length on the form. Some of them wrote minutes, some wrote mm:ss. I'd expect the figures to be messy."

Dariusz Mbeki (Agent, Billing Support): "I had a call that ran just under 40 minutes and the screen showed 0:00 for most of it. I took a note on paper."

4. Impact
Of the 212 affected calls, 141 have been matched to a complaint record. Complaint rate for the team on 13 October was reported at 3.9 per cent in the daily dashboard, based on 44 complaints from 1,140 calls.

Estimated correction: an earlier dashboard figure of 3.9 per cent was calculated on 1,140 calls. Following reconciliation, the answered-call count is 1,114, and the rate should read 4.0 per cent.

Call-length compliance check (policy QP-7.2, threshold 7 minutes 30 seconds for billing enquiries): the median manually recorded length on stations 14 to 22 was reported as 7 min 12 s. Recorded lengths are not yet validated.

5. Actions
- Recordings for affected calls to be reprocessed and reissued to Complaints Escalation by 22 October.
- Manual wrap-up field QA_DUR_MANUAL to be removed once patch is verified.
- Lorraine Feeney to brief Team C on mm:ss versus minutes entry standard.

Status: Open
Next review: 27 October 2026

Internal Policy Extract — Temperature Excursion Handling
Policy ref: QA-TEX-04 | Revision 3 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Quality Assurance, Harrowfield Depot

4. Temperature excursion rule

4.1 An excursion is any period in which a load recorded by the vehicle or dock logger leaves its set band: chilled loads +1°C to +5°C, frozen loads −18°C or colder.

4.2 Excursions are classed as Minor (under 30 minutes outside band, peak deviation no more than 2.0°C), Major (30 minutes or more outside band, or any deviation above 2.0°C), or Critical (any frozen load reading above −12°C).

4.3 On a Major or Critical excursion the driver must place the load on hold in the WMS and inform the duty QA officer by telephone within 15 minutes of the logger alarm.

4.4 Disposition of held loads is due within 3 working days of the excursion being logged. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays for the site.

4.5 Exception: where a load has been probed by a calibrated hand probe and the core reading is within band at the time of probing, the QA officer may downgrade a Major excursion to Minor. The downgrade must be recorded on form QA-F-19 with the probe serial number.

4.6 Exception: loads for export to a third-country customer are excluded from clause 4.5 and must be held regardless of probe result.

Schedule B — Logger readings are taken at 5-minute intervals. Where a logger has been replaced, readings from the replacement unit are not comparable with the earlier unit for the first 20 minutes.

RA-1 Scope
1.1 This clause applies to requests for teaching-free use of bookable rooms outside the published timetable, including examinations, society events, and visiting speaker sessions.
1.2 Requests must be submitted through the Room Request Form (RRF) no later than 10 working days before the requested date.

RA-2 Capacity and Allocation
2.1 Allocated capacity shall not exceed 85% of the room's fire-rated maximum occupancy as listed in the Estates Register.
2.2 Where two or more requests meet the criteria in RA-2.1, priority is given to the request with the earlier RRF timestamp.
2.3 Rooms in the Kestrel Building are bookable Monday to Friday, 08:00–20:30 only.

RA-3 Lead Time and Notice
3.1 Catering requests require 5 working days' notice to Facilities Services.
3.2 AV set-up requests require 3 working days' notice.
3.3 Cancellations received less than 2 working days before the event incur a £40 administration charge.

RA-4 Exceptions
4.1 The Head of Space Planning may waive RA-1.2 where the requesting department has a documented external deadline, provided the waiver is recorded against the RRF reference.
4.2 Exception 4.1 does not extend to catering notice under RA-3.1.

RA-5 Recording
5.1 Each allocation shall record the room reference, expected attendance, and the approver's initials.

1.1 MEWP hire shall be sourced from the approved hire list held by the site buyer.

Site: Harbour Point Contact Centre, Unit 3

Date of report: 28 October 2026

1. Background
On 22 October the BB-BILL queue recorded 14 complaints about mis-applied late-payment fees within 48 hours, against a policy trigger of 12 under QA-POL-07 section 4.2. This report reviews call records for the period 20 to 22 October and the handling of the affected calls.

2. Timeline (all times GMT)
07:52  Telephony platform reboot scheduled by NOC ticket NOC-88214. Notice sent to team leads at 07:40.
08:05  Agents on floors B and C report IVR stuck on prompt 6 (payment arrangement). Callers transferred directly to agent queue.
08:14  Team leader Sean Traynor logs incident in shift log, sheet reference SL-B-22/10.
08:31  Fee-waiver script v3.2 found not to load on desktop build 4.8.1. Agents using v3.1 from cached copy.
09:02  Platform restored. Queue volumes return to normal by 09:20.
09:47  Complaint intake team flags 6 complaints referencing a waived fee not reflected on statements.
11:30  Billing ops confirm 9 accounts affected by reversal failure on 21 October batch, not related to the platform fault.

3. Witness remarks
Sean Traynor (Team Leader, Floor B): "The reboot was on the notice board and in the team email. Two agents came in at 08:05 and didn't see either. I don't think anyone was told to stop using v3.2 before it went down, but the cache may have been pulling 3.1 since Tuesday."

Laszlo Ferreira-Dunn (Desktop Support): "v3.2 was live on the 19th. I checked the build log myself. Nothing in the cache was touched by the reboot. Agents were probably on 3.1 because their browsers were never cleared."

3. Call record figures
Calls handled on BB-BILL during the window: 1,840 across three shifts (Early 612, Late 701, Night 527).
Calls with a fee-waiver outcome recorded: 218 of 1,840 calls.
Complaints received referencing fee handling: 14.
Average handle time on affected calls: 6 min 42 sec.
Fee-waiver scripts reviewed in sampling: 40 calls, of which 31 followed the correct script version.

Note on correction: the figure for Late shift call volume in the 14:00 summary was entered as 701 in error. Corrected figure is 671. The shift total in section 3 should read accordingly.

4. Actions taken
- Script v3.2 pushed to all desktop builds by 29 October.
- Cache clear instruction issued to Floors B and C.
- Billing ops to re-apply 9 reversals in the 21 October batch.
- Complaint callbacks to 14 customers scheduled.

Hollin Brook Estate — Catering & Events Operations Manual
Section 7: Late Changes, Overruns and Supplier Exceptions
Document ref: HBE-OPS-07 (rev. 4, issued 14/03/2026)

7.1 Scope
This section applies to all events held at Hollin Brook Barn, the Orangery and the Walled Garden marquee, and to all catering supplied by Hollin Brook Kitchen or by approved external caterers.

7.2 Minimum notice for guest-number changes
(a) Guest-number increases must be notified to the Catering Manager no later than 10 working days before the event date.
(b) Decreases of up to 10% of the confirmed count may be made up to 5 working days before the event date without charge.
(c) Decreases greater than 10% are charged at 60% of the per-cover rate for the difference.

7.3 Marquee capacity
The Walled Garden marquee is rated for 180 seated guests with a single bar and 220 standing. Events exceeding seated capacity require written approval from the Operations Director under clause 7.7.

7.4 Cut-off for menu amendments
Menu amendments are accepted until 12:00 on the Friday preceding a Saturday event. Amendments received after this time are subject to a supplier surcharge of £14.50 per cover.

7.5 Overrun charges
Bar and catering staff are contracted to 01:00. Each additional 30 minutes or part thereof is charged at £275 plus VAT.

7.6 Supplier substitution
An approved external caterer may replace Hollin Brook Kitchen only where the Catering Manager has confirmed in writing that the substitute holds a current food hygiene rating of at least 4 and public liability cover of not less than £2 million.

7.7 Exception: Operations Director discretion
Clauses 7.2(a), 7.4 and 7.6 may be waived where the Operations Director approves in writing that the change is necessary for guest welfare, a bereavement, or a documented medical requirement. Approval must be recorded on the booking file before the event.

A call is classified as a formal complaint where the customer states dissatisfaction with a completed or ongoing service and asks for a response, a refund, or escalation. Calls logged with disposition code CMP-2 or CMP-3 are formal complaints.

QA-07.3 Response deadline
A formal complaint must receive a written acknowledgement within 2 working days of the call date. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays in England and Wales.

QA-07.4 Complaint rate reporting
Complaint rate is reported per site, per fortnight, as the number of formal complaints divided by the number of recorded calls handled in the same period, shown to one decimal place.

QA-07.5 Exception: repeat contact within 48 hours
Where a customer contacts the centre again about the same job reference within 48 hours of a call already classified under QA-07.2, the second call is recorded as a continuation and does not count as a new complaint, provided the agent confirmed the job reference and the first call's disposition code was recorded before the customer disconnected.

QA-07.6 Calibration
Team leaders must review a minimum of 12 calls per agent per fortnight. Calls under QA-07.5 are reviewed together with the originating call.

14.1 Scope

14.3 Goodwill credit
14.3.1 Agents may apply a goodwill credit of up to £75.00 without team leader approval.

Mrs Ferrier started a wash at 21:10 on Saturday 24/10/2026. The inlet hose had split at the elbow fitting behind the machine. Water ran onto the kitchen floor and through the gap by the back door into the dining room, and according to Callum it had stopped by the time he left at around 00:30 on Sunday, although he accepts he did not look behind the appliance. Release of Held Batches: Authority and Exceptions

4.1 A batch placed on QC hold under 4.3 may be released only by the Release Authority (RA) on the written recommendation of the Analytical Lead.

4.2 The RA shall not release a batch where any measured parameter exceeds its specification limit, save as provided in 4.5.

4.3 Hold status is applied automatically when a result is entered in LIMS with a flag of OOS or OOT. Hold status expires after 72 hours without a disposition entry, at which point the batch reverts to Quarantine (Q-status) and must be re-sampled.

4.4 Retained samples for a held batch shall be kept at 4 °C ±2 °C. Excursions outside this range shall be logged on Form QC-HT-02 within one working day.

4.5 EXCEPTION. The RA may release a batch carrying a parameter reading up to 0.5 mg/kg above specification for lead-free solder residue, provided that (a) a repeat test on a second aliquot falls within specification, (b) the customer's technical contact has been notified in writing, and (c) the deviation is recorded on Form QC-DV-11 with the reference number of the originating non-conformance.

4.6 Weekend and bank holiday entries are not counted toward the 72-hour period in 4.3 where the hold was applied on a Friday after 16:00 and the laboratory is closed.

1. Scope
1.1 This clause applies to all off-site educational visits arranged by staff and funded in whole or part from the school fund.
1.2 "Participating pupil" means a pupil on the trip roster on the date the deposit is paid.

2. Deposits and payments
2.1 A deposit of £25.00 per participating pupil is payable to the school office no later than 28 calendar days before departure.
2.2 Balance payments are due 14 days before departure. Late balance payments are subject to clause 4.3.
2.3 Visit leads must record each payment in the trip ledger on the day it is received.

3. Subsidy
3.1 The school fund may contribute up to £40.00 per pupil towards the total cost of a visit where the Head of Year has approved the visit in writing.
3.2 Where the subsidy is applied, the residual cost to the family must not exceed £60.00 per pupil.

4. Cancellation and refunds
4.1 Where a visit is cancelled by the school, all deposits and balance payments are refunded in full within 10 working days.
4.2 Where a family withdraws a pupil, the deposit is non-refundable unless the place can be filled from the reserve list (clause 4.4).
4.3 Late balance payments received after the due date may be refused at the Bursar's discretion, except where the family has an approved hardship application on file (see 4.5). Where a hardship application is on file, the late payment must be accepted and the pupil retained on the roster.
4.4 A reserve list of pupils may be maintained for each visit. A place may be offered from the reserve list only with the written agreement of the Head of Year.
4.5 Hardship applications must be countersigned by the Bursar and dated no later than the balance due date.

5.1 Visit leads must retain signed consent forms, payment ledgers and the Head of Year approval for six years.

Policy extract: QCL-POL-07 Batch Release and Retest Scheduling (Rev 4, effective 1 September 2026)

7.1 A batch may be released for despatch only on written sign-off by the Release Authority (QA Manager or named deputy).

7.2 Retest requests raised under 7.4 must be logged in LIMS within one working day of the failed result. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays for England and Wales.

Quality Control – Release Procedure QC-REL-04 (Rev 6)
Extract: Section 3, Conditional Batch Release

3.1 A batch may be recommended for release only when all tests listed in the batch specification sheet (BSS) have reported a result and that result is recorded in LIMS.

3.2 Where a microbiological result is pending, the batch shall be held in status QUARANTINE-M. The Release Authority (RA) may not release a held batch under any circumstance other than clause 3.4.

3.3 Stability retains are to be pulled at T+0, T+30 and T+90 days from date of manufacture. A retain sample not drawn within ±2 working days of its scheduled pull is recorded as a deviation (DEV) and reported to the Quality Manager within 1 working day.

3.4 Exception. A batch in QUARANTINE-M may be released conditionally if all of the following apply:
(a) the pending test is one of the non-critical panel (NCP-1 to NCP-7);
(b) the mean of the three duplicate plate counts for the pending test is at or below the limit in BSS table 4, and each individual count is no more than 1.5 times that limit;
(c) the Head of Microbiology has countersigned the conditional release form CRF-22;
(d) the batch is not destined for an infant or paediatric SKU.

3.5 Where clause 3.4 is not met, the RA shall either (i) retain the batch in QUARANTINE-M pending the full result, or (ii) reject the batch under QC-REL-09 if the result has already exceeded specification.

3.6 Conditional release under 3.4 is valid for 21 calendar days. After that period the batch reverts to QUARANTINE-M without further notice.

4. Room booking lead times and priority

4.1 Requests for teaching space must be submitted through the Room Booking Portal no less than 10 working days before the first session date.

4.2 Requests for examination space must be submitted no less than 15 working days before the examination date. Requests received inside this window are held in the Late Queue and allocated only after all in-window requests have been placed.

4.3 Rooms in the Harbourside Annex are bookable Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 19:30, and on Saturdays 09:00 to 13:00 only. No Sunday bookings are accepted at any site.

4.4 A room may not be allocated for more than 2 consecutive days to one module without written approval from the Head of Timetabling.

4.5 Where a booking spans midnight (for example a late-running laboratory session or an overnight equipment set-up), the booking is treated as two separate allocations, each of which is subject to clauses 4.3 and 4.4.

4.6 Exception: a booking request for a Level 6 or postgraduate practical assessment may be placed inside the 10-day window in 4.1 where the assessment is a formal requirement of a professional body. The requesting school must attach the professional body letter to the request.

5. Capacity and fit

5.1 A room is allocated only where its registered capacity is equal to or greater than the expected cohort. Registered capacity is the figure held in the Space Register, not the figure printed on the door.

5.2 Where the expected cohort exceeds registered capacity by more than 5 per cent, the request is returned to the school for re-scheduling.

5.3 Exception: rooms in the Clement Hall estate with a fixed-seat configuration may be allocated to cohorts up to 8 per cent above registered capacity where a seat-count audit dated within the previous 12 months confirms the figure.

Site: Northgate Distribution Centre, Unit 3 (Stock Control)

1. Background

I'm writing this up a bit longer than the form strictly asks for, because Gwen on the early shift asked me to put down everything we talked about on the Friday, not just the bits that went in the system. The short version is that the cycle count for bay family C (chilled overflow) didn't reconcile, and we spent most of the weekend arguing about whether the scanner handsets were at fault or the people. Anyway, here is the timeline as best I can reconstruct it from the WMS audit log (export ref WMS-EXP-88213) and from what people told me.

2. Timeline

Fri 23 Oct 06:40 — Early shift starts. Handset HH-07 reported "battery critical" at the dock door; swapped for HH-11.
Fri 23 Oct 09:15 — Cycle count C-14 commenced by M. Oduya and P. Tanaka.
Fri 23 Oct 11:52 — Count variance flagged on SKU 40217-CH (chilled yoghurt multipack). System 212 units, physical 186 units.
Fri 23 Oct 14:30 — Recount requested. Recount done by second pair; 186 units confirmed.
Fri 23 Oct 17:05 — Adjustment raised, then held pending investigation (ticket STK-6613).
Sat 24 Oct 01:30 — Overnight replen wave (wave 9) moved 40 cases into C-14 from the reserve racking. No record of the moved cases being scanned at putaway.
Mon 26 Oct 08:20 — Adjustment reviewed. Variance still open.

M. Oduya: "I'm fairly sure the handset was on HH-11 by then, the battery thing was on the Friday morning. I wouldn't put money on the exact minute."

P. Tanaka: "We did the count the way we always do it. If the cases went in at night without a scan, that's not on us. Nobody told us the wave was going into C-14."

Gwen Abara (early shift lead): "Honestly I think the overnight team were just pushing stuff to the nearest gap. It happens. I'd like someone to check the putaway logs before blaming the count."

Overnight team (not interviewed directly; remarks passed via shift handover sheet): "Wave 9 went where the system said. We scanned what we could."

4. Figures

The chilled overflow adjustment was recorded as a shortfall of 26 units on SKU 40217-CH. Of the 14 counts carried out in C-14 on 23 October, 3 showed a variance. Audit sample for the week of 19 October covered 58 scans from the same zone.

Note added 28 October following recount of the reserve racking: the shortfall figure in section 4 above is corrected to 19 units, not 26. The original figure was carried over from a draft adjustment sheet before the second recount was entered. The wave 9 case quantity in section 2 is unaffected.

Confirm handset HH-07 battery replacement (owner: Brandt).
Hold adjustment STK-6613 until 6 November.
